{{Quote|Your Highness, we must take this last transport. It's our only hope!|C-3PO, to Princess Leia Organa, during the Battle of Hoth|<ref name="ESB">{{Film|V}}</ref>}}
The '''''Bright Hope''''', also known as '''Transport C One Seven''', was a modified [[Gallofree Yards, Inc./Legends|Gallofree Yards]] [[GR-75 medium transport/Legends|GR-75 medium transport]] that saw service with the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] during the height of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. Acquired as one of several outdated and dilapidated [[Transport/Legends|transports]] by the Rebellion, the ''Bright Hope'' nevertheless played an invaluable role in the rapid transit of war matériel. By [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], the [[Starship/Legends|ship]] was one of thirty GR-75 transports stationed at the [[Alliance High Command/Legends|Alliance High Command]] headquarters of [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]]. As the final transport to evacuate the besieged base late during the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], the ''Bright Hope'' carried an overloaded number of wounded and [[Death/Legends|dying]] passengers in its attempt to run the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]] of the planet. The ship was disabled and all but destroyed by concentrated fire from Imperial [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]] and the [[Mist Hunter/Legends|''Mist Hunter'']], the craft of the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] [[Zuckuss/Legends|Zuckuss]] and [[4-LOM/Legends|4-LOM]]. Due to the efforts of Echo Base's chief controller, [[Toryn Farr/Legends|Toryn Farr]], the ''Bright Hope''{{'s}} 108 surviving passengers were safely recovered.

==Description==
The ''Bright Hope'' was typical of the [[Gallofree Yards, Inc./Legends|Gallofree Yards]]<ref name="NEGVV" /><ref name="BTM" /><ref name="TSSE" /> [[GR-75 medium transport/Legends|GR-75 medium transport]]<ref name="SWCL" /> line.<ref name="NEGVV" /> At only ninety [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in length, the [[Clam/Legends|clamshell]]-shaped [[Transport/Legends|transport]] could nonetheless haul a considerable amount of cargo for its size, at up to 19,000 metric tons.<ref name="NEGVV" /><ref name="EGVV" /> Modular cargo pods were located at the front and underside of the outer hull, each equipped with a [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] device for rapid loading and unloading, and secured in place and protected against [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] and [[Vacuum/Legends|vacuum]] by an invisible [[Magnetic field/Legends|magnetic shield]],<ref name="NEGVV" /> while the vessel's interior was equipped to hold additional cargo and could comfortably house about ninety passengers.<ref name="BTM" />

Perched above the top of the outer hull was the stalked, cramped command pod, where a crew of seven&mdash;including a command crew of six and one [[Gunner/Legends|gunner]]&mdash;operated the [[Starship/Legends|ship]].<ref name="BTM" /> The transport's single rudimentary [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|deflector shield generator]] was also located within the pod, protecting a vital yet dangerously exposed section of the vessel.<ref name="NEGVV" /> The ''Bright Hope'' could alternatively function with a skeleton crew of three.<ref name="TSSE" /> The gunner controlled<ref name="BTM" /> the ship's minimal armament of four retractable,<ref name="NEGVV" /> fire-linked twin [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannons]],<ref name="TSSE" /> though the ''Bright Hope'', like all GR-75 medium transports, was largely unfit for combat. Instead, the ''Bright Hope'' typically relied on the escort of [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] for protection while moving between [[Star system/Legends|star systems]], a long-range [[Sensor/Legends|sensor]] suite and advanced countermeasure systems for detecting and escaping enemy ships, as well as extensive [[Durasteel/Legends|durasteel]]<ref name="NEGVV" /> [[Armor/Legends|armored]] plating<ref name="BTM" /> that showed the wear and tear of [[Standard year/Legends|years]] of use.<ref name="SWCL" />

[[File:Brighthopeicwsw.jpg|thumb|left|275px|The ''Bright Hope'', stationed inside Echo Base]]
The ''Bright Hope'' was propelled by three standard primary [[Sublight engine/Legends|sublight]] [[Ion engine/Legends|ion drive]] [[Engine/Legends|engines]] and six secondary drive engines,<ref name="BTM" /><ref name="EGVV" /> powered by a main [[Reactor/Legends|reactor]],<ref name="NEGVV" /> and was also outfitted with a standard Class 4.0 [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] for [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] travel.<ref name="BTM" /> The ''Bright Hope''{{'s}} engines, like those of its GR-75 brothers, were greater in number than its civilian-use predecessor, the [[GR-45 medium transport/Legends|GR-45 medium transport]], to provide greater power.<ref name="SWCL" /> The transport had a maximum acceleration of 900 G,<ref name="NEGVV" /> and a maximum speed of twenty [[megalight]]s in [[Realspace/Legends|space]]<ref name="BTM" /> and up to 650 [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] per [[Standard hour/Legends|hour]] in atmosphere. Four retractable landing gear legs extending from the underside of the ship,<ref name="NEGVV" /> along with repulsorlift drive units and a retractable [[Entry ramp/Legends|boarding ramp]], made landing on [[Planet/Legends|planetary]] surfaces a possibility.<ref name="BTM" /><ref name="OPF" />

The transport's interior was mostly hollow, consisting of at least three modular decks, interchangeably equipped to hold either passengers or cargo.<ref name="SWCL" /> By the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]], the ''Bright Hope'' was modified with expanded passenger capacity to facilitate evacuation.<ref name="CCL" /> It was arranged with two freight decks at the bottom of the ship and a single passenger deck near the top. Ladders connected the decks.<ref name="OPF" /> The passenger deck module consisted of columns of adjacent seats running four across and facing another set of four separated by a common walkway. Each group of eight inward-facing seats were in turn separated by consoles.<ref name="SWCL" />

The ''Bright Hope'' featured a centralized [[Computer/Legends|computer]] system accessible from throughout the ship, including a Ship's Registry database for data on other starships. The ''Bright Hope''{{'s}} bulkheads were fitted with small storage compartments, some of which by [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]] held [[Bantha wool/Legends|bantha wool]] [[Blanket/Legends|blankets]] and [[Color/Legends|white]] [[Pillow/Legends|pillows]], and the inner passageways were lighted by a standard illumination system and a dim emergency system that offered light from the ceiling, powered by [[Power cell/Legends|power cells]] on each level of the ship. Emergency power supplies were also available. [[Viewport/Legends|Viewports]] at intervals offered vistas of the surrounding outside environment. At least three [[Escape pod/Legends|escape pods]], each capable of carrying six passengers, were located on the passenger deck.<ref name="OPF" /> The ''Bright Hope'' carried six [[Standard month/Legends|months]] of consumables.<ref name="TSSE" />

==History==
===Acquisition and assignment to Echo Base===
The ''Bright Hope'' was constructed by Gallofree Yards sometime before the corporation's dissolution in [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]]. It was one of many GR-75 medium transports obtained by the Rebel Alliance at a bargain price for cargo transportation duties. Although outdated and dilapidated by the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the Gallofree transports were instrumental in helping the Rebellion to efficiently move valuable matériel ranging from medicine to weapons.<ref name="EGVV" /> GR-75 medium transports like the ''Bright Hope'' were invaluable in helping Rebel bases quickly evacuate in the face of an impending [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] assault as early as the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]].<ref name="SWCL" />

By 3 ABY, the ''Bright Hope'' was stationed at the [[Alliance High Command/Legends|Alliance High Command]] headquarters' secret [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] on the remote ice world of [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]]. It was among a [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] of thirty GR-75 medium transports transferred to Hoth to supplement the needs of the facility. The ''Bright Hope'' occupied a position at the north-west corner of Echo Base's interior, within the central transport [[Hangar/Legends|hangar]] at the end of a column of similarly immobile GR-75 transports lining the western-most ice wall. When not in use, the transport was routinely kept connected to one of the base's many [[Power generator/Legends|power generators]].<ref name="SWCL" />

===Battle of Hoth===
{{Main|Battle of Hoth/Legends}}
{{Quote|Transport, this is Solo. Better take off. I can't get to you. I'll get her out on the ''Falcon''.|Han Solo, after a cave-in prevented Princess Leia Organa from reaching the ''Bright Hope''|<ref name="ESB" />}}
Following the discovery of an Imperial [[Arakyd Industries/Legends|Arakyd]] [[Viper probe droid/Legends|Viper probe droid]] and the arrival of [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader's]] [[Death Squadron/Legends|fleet]] of [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers]], the [[Death Squadron/Legends|Death Squadron]], in the [[Hoth system/Legends|Hoth system]], the Rebel forces of Echo Base began a hasty retreat of their compromised outpost. The base became a hodgepodge of frantic scurrying, with people rushing to load whatever vital equipment onto the base's transports they could muster before they were forced to evacuate. The [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] of [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Group]] were tasked with engaging and delaying the advance of the Imperial [[Walker/Legends|walker]] invasion force in order to buy time for the base's transports to escape.<ref name="GG3">[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back'', Second Edition]]</ref>

[[File:SouthSlopeStagingArea.jpg|thumb|right|300px|The ''Bright Hope'' lifts off from the [[South Ridge/Legends|South Slope]] staging area.]]
The transports, unable to defend themselves against the might of Vader's blockading Death Squadron, would be escorted by two starfighters through the Imperial line. Additionally, the evacuation plan called for the base's [[V-150 Planet Defender/Legends|v-150 anti-orbital ion cannon]] to provide suppressing covering fire to clear a flight path for the transports to slip by, enter [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]], and escape to the Rebels' predetermined [[Haven (rendezvous point)|rendezvous point]] beyond the [[Galactic Rim/Legends|rim]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="GG3" /> Given its docking position in the hangar farthest from the staging area, the ''Bright Hope'' would by default be the final transport to attempt evacuation.<ref name="SWCL" /> Since no one would be left behind to man the [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannon]] to provide cover for the ''Bright Hope'', the last remaining Echo Base personnel planned to set the cannon on autofire and simply make a run for it.<ref name="ESB radio">[[The Empire Strikes Back (radio)|''The Empire Strikes Back'' radio drama]]</ref>

As the Battle of Hoth raged, the transports lifted off, one by one, from the evacuation staging area just behind the [[South Ridge/Legends|South Ridge]], beyond the south entrance of Echo Base.<ref name="SWCL" /> The ''Bright Hope'' was intended to be the evacuation transport assigned to [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]], as she steadfastly remained in the base's command center to direct the final actions of the battle and to ensure that the last remnants remaining in the base reached their own escape ships.<ref name="ESB novel" /> As an indicator of their subtle yet increasingly blossoming attachment to each other, [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] risked his own safety to escort Organa and the [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] to the ''Bright Hope''{{'s}} docking hangar. When they were cut off en route by an ice avalanche in one of the base's corridors from the explosions of the battle outside, Solo instead was forced to oversee her escape aboard his own ship, the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']], instructing the ''Bright Hope'' to lift off in light of their inability to reach the transport.<ref name="ESB" />

===Running the gauntlet===
{{Quote|Let's give our Imperial friends a seventeenth ship.|Zuckuss, announcing his intentions to destroy the fleeing ''Bright Hope''|<ref name="OPF" />}}
As the last transport remaining, the ''Bright Hope'' was, appropriately enough, the last beacon of hope for the hundreds of Rebel personnel still on the planet. [[Toryn Farr/Legends|Toryn Farr]], Echo Base's chief controller and the final person to evacuate the command center, was one of the many who were reliant on the ship as a means to escape. By the time she reached the hangar and saw the transport's flight deck, the scene before her was a motley assortment of many wounded and dying people being assisted by [[Medical droid/Legends|medical droids]]. With the Imperial advance having already breached the walls of the base, Farr realized the grim predicament facing all those present. She saw no conceivable way of getting all the wounded onto the ship while still allowing the ''Bright Hope'' enough time to safely take off.<ref name="OPF" />

[[File:Brighthope.jpg|thumb|left|225px|The ''Bright Hope'' leaves [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]].]]
When a group of [[Cold assault stormtrooper|snowtroopers]] began firing on the hangar from the corridor behind her, Farr inadvertently took up a defensive position behind a crate of [[Thermal detonator/Legends|thermal detonators]]. Noticing its contents, she tore open the crate and used the explosives to halt the Imperial advance, creating a cave-in that choked off the corridor. Farr thus bought the valuable time needed to get the remaining wounded soldiers aboard the transport, including her sister, [[Samoc Farr/Legends|Samoc Farr]]. Among those who boarded the final evacuation ship was [[Colonel/Legends|Colonel]] [[Ledick Firest/Legends|Ledick Firest]], who stayed behind to oversee the final disengagement of [[Alliance Army/Legends|Rebel troops]] from the battlefield.<ref name="GG3" /> The ''Bright Hope'' lifted off from the hangar, leaving behind tons of vital equipment in lieu of the unanticipated number of overloaded passengers, with moments to spare as more snowtroopers descended on the hangar from the snow fields outside.<ref name="OPF" /> As a transport designed to safely carry ninety individuals, the ''Bright Hope'' blasted away from Hoth carrying hundreds.<ref name="SWCL" />

The ''Bright Hope'' held the distinction of being escorted by six [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing starfighters]] as it made its desperate run through the blockading line of [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyers]], including fighters piloted by [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]], [[Derek Klivian/Legends|Derek Klivian]], [[Wes Janson/Legends|Wes Janson]],<ref name="SWCL" /> and [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] [[Tarn Mison]],<ref name="SEL">{{CCG|set=Special Edition Limited|cardname=Lieutenant Tarn Mison}}</ref> though the base's ion cannon had long been neutralized at this point.<ref name="GG3" /> Even the ship's uniquely heavy escort could not save it from the armada of Imperial [[Warship/Legends|warships]] waiting for the final transport. The ''Bright Hope'' was damaged and nearly destroyed by the [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|Super Star Destroyer]] [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']]<ref name="OPF" /> and the [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer]] ''[[Stalker/Legends|Stalker]]''.<ref name="CCL" /> Additionally, the ''Bright Hope'' was intercepted by the [[G-1A starfighter/Legends|G-1A transport]] [[Mist Hunter/Legends|''Mist Hunter'']], the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunting]] craft of the [[Gand/Legends|Gand]] [[Zuckuss/Legends|Zuckuss]] and the [[LOM-series protocol droid/Legends|LOM-series protocol droid]] [[4-LOM/Legends|4-LOM]], who had come to the Hoth [[Star system/Legends|system]] on an Imperial assignment. Having exited hyperspace in time to encounter the end of the [[Space warfare/Legends|space battle]], the [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]]-hunting duo hoped to destroy the ''Bright Hope'' as a token of good will to their Imperial employers. The ''Mist Hunter'' wiped out the perched command pod, while the two Star Destroyers ripped into the transport's hull, exposing three decks to the [[Vacuum/Legends|vacuum]] of [[Realspace/Legends|space]]. Drifting helpless and without power, the ''Bright Hope'' went down as the seventeenth GR-75 medium transport caught in the blockade's snare.<ref name="OPF" />

===A last hope===
Although a badly damaged wreck of a ship&mdash;a large portion of the vessel had completely broken away&mdash;the ''Bright Hope'' still held pockets able to sustain life. The two freight decks were still completely intact, and the remaining passenger deck was 17.4% intact with over four [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]] of breathable [[Oxygen/Legends|oxygen]] left. The intact portions of the ship had been sealed off by emergency containment [[Deflector shield/Legends|shields]] where the destroyed section of the ship had exploded away. While the ship's depressurization had been quick, most of the ''Bright Hope''{{'s}} passengers had been sucked out into vacuum. Still, survivors remained, among them Toryn Farr.<ref name="OPF" />

[[File:Toryn-hd.png|thumb|right|205px|Echo Base Chief Controller Toryn Farr led the ''Bright Hope''{{'s}} 108 survivors to safety.]]

Farr discovered a total of 108 passengers alive&mdash;eight pilots, thirty-two newly inducted soldiers, support staff from the command center, hangar crew, personnel with specialized [[Hunting/Legends|hunting]] and survival skills, and one cook&mdash;though fifty-two were badly wounded. Some of the Echo Base survivors included Rebels [[Rory]], [[Seito]], [[Bindu]], [[Darklighter (Bright Hope)|Darklighter]], [[Crimmins]], [[Sala Natu]], [[Meghan Rivers]], and [[Berec Tanaal]]. As the ranking officer among the survivors, Farr assumed command of her comrades. They salvaged three operational [[Escape pod/Legends|escape pods]], grimly determining that they would only be able to hold eighteen individuals. To complicate matters, the group identified an ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer having begun mop-up duties of similarly destroyed vessels floating in space nearby. With time running out, Farr selected four of the ''Bright Hope''{{'s}} survivors&mdash;Seito, Crimmins, Sala Natu, and Berec Tanaal&mdash;as those most valuable to the Rebellion's cause, who might also be fit enough to survive Hoth's harsh climate, to occupy positions in the escape pods. The remaining fourteen individuals to join them in the escape pods were nominated and voted on by the rest of the transport's survivors. The eighteen chosen were jettisoned back to Hoth in the hope that they would survive long enough for later retrieval<ref name="OPF" />&mdash;it was better to risk the cold and attacks from Hoth's native [[Wampa/Legends|wampas]] than face Imperial interrogation and [[Prison/Legends|imprisonment]].<ref name="Fact File 33">{{FactFile|33|HOT 13-16|Escape of the Rebels}}</ref>

With incarceration or [[Death/Legends|death]] at the hands of the Empire looming heavily on the minds of the remaining passengers, Farr, with the assistance of a dedicated [[Bright Hope hacker droid|hacker droid]] attached to the transport's central [[Computer/Legends|computer]], dutifully erased the computer records and [[Droid/Legends|droids]] aboard, lest information regarding those who had served at Echo Base and had escaped aboard the ''Bright Hope'' fall into Imperial hands. It was then that the ''Mist Hunter'' returned and docked with the ''Bright Hope'', with the bounty hunters Zuckuss and 4-LOM hoping to board the transport to capture and collect the bounties on twenty-six of the most valuable surviving Rebels aboard. After a few tense moments of negotiation between Zuckuss and 4-LOM and the Rebels aboard the ''Bright Hope'', Farr, carrying the highest price on her head among the survivors, convinced the hunters to instead rescue the remaining ninety passengers, including the medical droids [[2-1B/Legends|2-1B]]<ref name="OPF" /> and [[FX-7/Legends|FX-7]],<ref name="BTM" /><ref name="Who's Who">{{InsiderCite|74|Who's Who in Echo Base: The Unsung Rebels of the Battle of Hoth}}</ref> and deliver them to the sanctuary of the Rebel underground on the nearby planet [[Darlyn Boda/Legends|Darlyn Boda]].<ref name="OPF" />

The ''Bright Hope''{{'s}} crippled remains were left to float through space, free for the Imperial fleet to search, though little information was left behind for their benefit.<ref name="OPF" /> The eighteen members who were jettisoned from the ''Bright Hope'' back to Hoth were eventually recovered by an [[Alliance Special Forces/Legends|Alliance Special Forces]] team led by Toryn Farr.<ref name="BTM" />

==Behind the scenes==
===Notable appearances===
The ''Bright Hope'' was first featured in the short story "[[Of Possible Futures: The Tale of Zuckuss and 4-LOM]]," written by author [[M. Shayne Bell]] as part of the [[December]] [[1996]] anthology book ''[[Tales of the Bounty Hunters]]''. The story provided a name and expanded operational history for the transport Han Solo attempts to bring Princess Leia Organa to during the Battle of Hoth in the [[1980]] film [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']]. The ''Bright Hope''{{'s}} name is effectively derived from C-3PO's spoken film line, suggesting to the Princess that the final transport is their "only hope" for escape.<ref name="OPF" /><ref name="ESB" />

The [[1998]] [[Wikipedia:Personal computer|PC]] program ''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]'' later established the GR-75 medium transport lifting off from the staging area outside Echo Base in the background scene in which [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] boards his X-wing to evacuate Hoth in ''The Empire Strikes Back'' as the ''Bright Hope'', thus [[Retroactive continuity|retconning]] the film as the ship's first [[canon]]ical appearance.<ref name="BTM" />

===Inconsistencies===
There are several inconsistencies regarding the ''Bright Hope''.

According to the second edition of the [[West End Games]] sourcebook [[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back'']], the transport Leia Organa was assigned to board was the [[Thon's Orchard/Legends|''Thon's Orchard'']].<ref name="GG3" /> Additionally, in the [[The Empire Strikes Back (radio)|radio adaptation]] of ''The Empire Strikes Back'', Luke Skywalker informs Organa that he will be escorting her transport&mdash;the last flight to leave.<ref name="ESB radio" /> ''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]'', however, describes Skywalker as escorting the GR-75 medium transport piloted by [[Tarrin Datch/Legends|Tarrin Datch]],<ref name="EGC">''[[The Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> which ''Galaxy Guide 3'' identifies as the ''Thon's Orchard''&mdash;one of the final transports to leave, though not the last&mdash;a ship that successfully made the run through the Imperial blockade of Hoth.<ref name="GG3" /> To further compound the confusion, the transport piloted by Datch in ''The Empire Strikes Back'' radio adaptation is intended to be the final evacuation transport.<ref name="BTM" /><ref name="ESB radio" />

Another inconsistency arises with the script of ''The Empire Strikes Back'' radio adaptation, published in ''[[The Empire Strikes Back: The National Public Radio Dramatization]]'', which identifies the last evacuation transport as the ship assigned to [[General/Legends|General]] [[Carlist Rieekan/Legends|Carlist Rieekan]].<ref name="ESB radio script">[[The Empire Strikes Back: The National Public Radio Dramatization|''The Empire Strikes Back'': The National Public Radio Dramatization]]</ref> This is contradicted by "Of Possible Futures: The Tale of Zuckuss and 4-LOM," which places Rieekan at the rendezvous point ahead of the ''Bright Hope''{{'s}} crew.<ref name="OPF" />

''Star Wars: Behind the Magic'' and the reference book [[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']] both identify the ''Bright Hope'' as the transport seen lifting off from the staging area outside Echo Base in the background shot when Luke Skywalker departs Hoth in ''The Empire Strikes Back''. This seems to contradict "Of Possible Futures," which describes the ''Bright Hope'' as lifting off directly from the base's hangar.<ref name="BTM" /><ref name="SWCL" />

In the [[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|novelization of ''The Empire Strikes Back'']], Han Solo refers to the ship as "Transport C One Seven," which this article treats as a registry number.<ref name="ESB novel" /> [[The Official Star Wars Fact File 48|''The Official Star Wars Fact File'' 48]] erroneously identifies the ''Bright Hope'' as the "'''''Bright Star'''''."<ref name="Fact File 48">{{FactFile|48|BOU 9-10|Bounty Hunters &ndash; 4-LOM}}</ref> In "Of Possible Futures," there is some uncertainty as to which medical droid accompanies 2-1B aboard the ''Bright Hope''. Author M. Shayne Bell inexplicably alternates between referring to 2-1B's partner as "Effour-Seven" and "Effex-Seven" all within the course of several paragraphs.<ref name="OPF" /> However, ''Star Wars: Behind the Magic'' and the article "[[Who's Who in Echo Base: The Unsung Rebels of the Battle of Hoth|Who's Who in Echo Base]]" from [[Star Wars Insider 74|''Star Wars Insider'' 74]] both identify the droid as FX-7,<ref name="BTM" /><ref name="Who's Who" /> the most traditionally accepted counterpart of 2-1B, as seen in ''The Empire Strikes Back''.<ref name="ESB" />
